products.name: Grammarly for Education
products.note: Institutional writing support; student data; FERPA compliance; generative AI features

profile_text.body:
Grammarly is a for-profit company founded in 2009 and headquartered in San Francisco, California. Its website describes it as an AI writing assistance platform that provides personalized guidance, text generation, grammar correction, tone adjustment, and style suggestions across any app or website. The company states that it does not sell or monetize user content, provide it for advertising purposes, or allow third-party service providers to train their models on user content.

The company offers two tracked products: Grammarly, a general writing and editing tool that reads document text broadly, and Grammarly for Education, an institutional product designed for student writing support that includes generative AI features and is described as FERPA-compliant. The site claims that organizations deploying Grammarly save an average of $5,000 per employee per year, and references a productivity offering called Superhuman Go that combines writing support with what the company describes as productivity agents.

The held facts note 139 instances of California law exposure associated with the company, consistent with its San Francisco headquarters. No litigation cases or MCP server registrations are currently recorded for Grammarly in the site's holdings.
